notes.text: All the prophets — Of Baal.

Jezebel sent — She gives him notice of it before hand: partly, out of the height of her spirit, as scorning to kill him secretly: partly, out of her impatience, till she had breathed out her rage: and principally, from God's all-disposing providence, that so he might have an opportunity of escaping. Do to me, &c. - So far was she from being changed by that evident miracle, that she persists in her former idolatry, and adds to it a monstrous confidence, that in spight of God she would destroy his prophet.
Left his servant — Because he would not expose him to those perils and hardships which he expected: and because he desired solitude, that he might more freely converse with God.

Into the wilderness — The vast wilderness of Arabia. He durst not stay in Judah, tho' good Jehosaphat reigned there, because he was allied to Ahab, and was a man of an easy temper, whom Ahab might circumvent, and either by force or art seize upon Elijah. It is enough - I have lived long enough for thy service, and am not like to do thee any more service; neither my words nor works are like to do any good upon these unstable and incorrigible people. I am not better - That I should continue in life, when other prophets who have gone before me, have lost their lives.

Angel of the Lord, &c. — He needed not to complain of the unkindness of men, when it was thus made up by the ministration of angels. Wherever God's children are, they are still under their father's eye.

And went — He wandered hither and thither for forty days, 'till at last he came to Horeb, which in the direct road was not above three or four days journey. Thither the spirit of the Lord led him, probably beyond his own intention, that he might have communion with God, in the same place that Moses had.
Unto a cave — Perhaps the same wherein Moses was hid when the Lord passed before him, and proclaimed his name.

I have been, &c. — I have executed my office with zeal for God's honour, and with the hazard of my own life, and am fled hither, not being able to endure to see the dishonour done to thy name by their obstinate idolatry and wickedness. I only - Of all thy prophets, who boldly and publickly plead thy cause: for the rest of thy prophets who are not slain, hide themselves, and dare not appear to do thee any service. They seek my life - I despair of doing them any good: for instead of receiving my testimony, they hunt for my life. It does by no means appear, that he was at all to blame, for fleeing from Jezebel. If they persecute you in one city flee into another. Besides, the angels feeding and preparing him for his journey, and the peculiar blessing of God upon that food, indicated the divine approbation.

And behold — This is a general description of the thing, after which the manner of it is particularly explained. Strong wind - Whereby he both prepares Elijah to receive this discovery of God with greatest humility, reverence, and godly fear; and signifies his irresistible power, to break the hardest hearts of the Israelites, and to bear down all opposition that was or should be made against him in the discharge of his office. The Lord was not - The Lord did not vouchsafe his special and gracious presence to Elijah in that wind, which possibly was to teach him not to wonder if God did not accompany his terrible administration at mount Carmel with the presence of his grace, to turn the hearts of the Israelites to himself.

A still voice — To intimate, that God would do his work in and for Israel in his own time, not by might or power, but by his own spirit, Zech iv, 6, which moves with a powerful, but yet with a sweet and gentle gale.

He wrapped, &c. — Through dread of God's presence, being sensibly that he was neither worthy nor able to endure the sight of God with open face. And stood, &c. - Which God commanded him to do; and as he was going towards the mouth of the cave, he was affrighted and stopped in his course, by the dreadful wind, and earthquake, and fire; when these were past, he prosecutes his journey, and goeth on to the mouth of the cave.

glossa.text: *Elias therefore was afraid, and rising up he went away,* etc. ((RAB.)) Holy men, the spirit lifting them up, are caught away to the highest things: but so long as they are in this life, lest they be proud, they are held down by temptations. Hence it is that Elias, when he had gone forward with so many virtues, afterwards fled from Jezabel, a queen indeed, yet a mere woman: and he who raised the dead, foresaw things to come, did other glorious things also, struck with fear, flees death from the hand of a woman, seeks death from the hand of God, and receives it not.
*And behold an angel of the Lord touched him.* ((RAB.)) The angel who fed Elias signifies the angel of great counsel; by whose work we subsist both in bodily and in spiritual nature.

*And behold at his head,* etc. ((ID.)) Elias twice fed expresses the infirmity of our nature, for whom a single feeding does not suffice, but a double, that we may be able to ascend to things above. For as the body cannot subsist without bodily food, so neither can the soul live without the word of God.

((ID.)) So we also, when we shake off from us the sleep of sloth, must needs, being strengthened by divine comfort, hasten with all our might, by the step of good works, through all the time of the present life, to ascend into the mountain of God and into his holy place, that there we may find eternal rest.

*And a wind.* ((ID.)) A wind before the Lord overthrows mountains and breaks rocks in pieces, etc., *as far as* to begin to go forth to the knowledge of the truth.

*Not in the wind.* That is, think not that the Lord comes with the wind, but after the wind of commotion, that is, the whirlwind and the rush of the wind, fire shall pass by, then a whistling of a thin air, after this the Lord shall pass by, that he may speak with thee.

*I only,* etc. ((RAB.)) What was hard for so great a prophet to know, that servants had remained to God in this world? But he who, being humble, had known even the hidden things of God, being lifted up knew not even the open things. Whence it is certain that he enlightens himself with a ray of humility who subtly weighs the good things of others: because while he beholds outwardly, and in others, the things which he himself has done, he presses down that swelling of pride which strives to break forth within out of singularity. Hence it is that by the voice of God it is said to Elias, who reckoned himself alone. *I have left me seven thousand men,* that while he knew that not he alone had remained, he might bow down the glory of elation which was rising in him out of singularity.

((RAB.)) Not otherwise, save that he foretold that he should be king. Eliseus not otherwise than by casting his mantle upon him. Those two kings neither he himself in person, nor Eliseus his disciple, anointed, but a certain one of the prophets was sent to anoint Jehu.

notes.text: Panteth — After the enjoyment of thee in thy sanctuary.
Thirsteth — Not after vain useless idols, but after the only true and living God. Appear - In the place of his special presence and publick worship.

Remember — My banishment from God's presence, and mine enemies triumphs. In me - I breathe out my sorrows and complaints to God within my own breast. The multitudes - Israelites, who went thither in great numbers. Holy-day - Or that kept the feast, the three solemn festival solemnities, which they kept holy unto the Lord.

For — Hebrew. for the salvations of his face, for those supports, deliverances and comforts which I doubt not I shall enjoy both in his presence and sanctuary, and from his presence, and the light of his countenance.

Therefore — Therefore that I may revive my drooping spirits. Remember - I will consider thy infinite mercy and power, and faithfulness. Mizar - From all the parts of the land, to which I shall be driven; whether from the parts beyond Jordan on the east: or mount Hermon, which was in the northern parts.

Deep — One affliction comes immediately after another, as if it were called for by the former. A metaphor taken from violent and successive showers of rain; which frequently come down from heaven, as it were at the noise, or call of God's water spouts.
Command — Will effectually confer upon me. Loving-kindness - His blessings, the effects of his loving-kindness.
As — As a sword, which cutteth the very bones, so painful are their reproaches. The psalmist appeals to God, ver. 1, 2. Prays to be restored to the public ordinances, and trusts in God, ver. 3-5.

glossa.text:
*As the hart desireth,* etc. ((AUG.)) This voice suits catechumens, and also all who are still journeying abroad.

*The hart.* The hart, burdened with age, its hairs and horns growing out, draws in a serpent by its nostrils: whence, burning with the venom, it most ardently desires a fountain from which to drink; and when it has drunk, it lays aside its horns and its hairs.

*It hath thirsted.* ((AUG.)) He determines his desire, because the hart could be understood to desire a fountain for the sake of drinking, or of washing; here all desire is shown to be toward God. *When shall I come.* What is quicker to God is slow to the desire of man. Such a hart, while it runs, suffers those who insult; whence: *My tears have been my bread.* In prosperity also, which he despises, as in adversity. *Bread.* ((CASS.)) Not bitterness, or destruction, but *bread.*

*These things I remembered.* ((AUG.)) While they ask, Where is thy God? I also have meditated through all these visible things, and through my own soul, that through those outward things I may find the invisible things of God. Behold the understanding of the title. *I poured out. ((Ibid.))* For understanding and attaining I have spread it out above itself. *I poured out.* ((CASS.)) Or, I have rejoiced. My soul is melted within me; not outside, but pricked with compunction it returns into itself. Although I do not see God visibly, yet I consider that through the Church, in which the saints are wonderful, I shall come to the heavenly Jerusalem, taken captive by the sweetness of the angelic praise, which is received by the mind. *Into the place of the tabernacle.* ((AUG.)) The tabernacle of God on earth, etc., *as far as,* that is, of those rejoicing in the eternal refreshment. *In the voice of exultation. ((Ibid.))* Of the eternal festival there sounds something sweet to the heart: whence the hart is snatched away to the fountains of waters, and is soothed. But because the world makes a din, and the flesh weighs down the soul, comparing this sorrow with those joyful things, he says:

*Why art thou sad?* etc. ((CASS.)) Of the disturbances against which reason strengthens the sensual soul with hope of God. *Why dost thou trouble?* ((AUG.)) Who, if thou searchest, there is nothing in the world for which thou shouldst owe this: hope rather for the saving remedy still, and if not now, fully in time to come. *Hope.* ((CASS.)) Or he can hope, because *still* in the present *I will confess,* that is, I will do penance for my sins, that I may not withstand thee.

*To myself.* Turned to God he tells the troublings from himself, the end of them from God: whence in him is his hope. And this is *to myself,* or from myself. ((CASS.)) Behold, he who above was correcting the soul to the condition of man, having turned back says here that the soul is troubled by itself, which, were there not the vices of the flesh, would remain tranquil. Behold out of what diversity man is composed. As if: therefore, that is, on account of the troublings of the soul, *I will be mindful.* ((AUG.)) That is, I hasten to thee, because thou shuttest out all evils. Behold the remedy by which he may escape the troublings: whence he subjoins for what things he is mindful: *Of the land of Jordan,* where the Lord consecrated baptism, in which the humbled are washed, and become fruitful earth. ((CASS.)) He who is mindful of these things is not troubled by evils. *Therefore mindful.* ((AUG.)) Whereby the soul is troubled toward me, therefore *mindful,* etc. No one runs to remission, save he who is displeasing to himself, save he who confesses himself a sinner: which *Hermoniim* denotes; no one confesses unless he humbles himself, which is denoted in *the little one. Jordan. ((Ibid.))* A going down. Descend therefore that thou mayest be lifted up. ((CASS.)) In the Jordan the Lord consecrated baptism, in which the humbled are washed, and become fruitful earth, which yields fruit thirtyfold, sixtyfold and a hundredfold ((Matth. XIII)). *Hermoniim.* ((AUG.)) A small mountain beside the Jordan, etc., *as far as* because it is not among the proud, but among the humble, that one is mindful of God.

*Deep unto deep. ((Ibid.))* It is fitting that I be mindful, etc., *as far as* and on account of all these things I pray in adversities, and this is: *With me a prayer. ((Ibid.))* Or *deep calleth unto deep,* that is, the judgment which God brought upon the sinner, etc., *as far as* because he fears the judgments. *Of the cataracts.* Cataracts, according to the letter, are the mouths of rivers.
*In the day. ((Ibid.))* That is, in prosperity, etc., *as far as* whence we may live in adversity. *With me a prayer. ((Ibid.))* Prayer in troublings is mine, and this is with me.
*Why hast thou forgotten.* ((CASS.)) Why dost thou now suffer me to be vexed with these miseries? He saw what sweetness of the fatherland there was, and shuddered at the perils of the world.

*While my bones are broken.* ((AUG.)) As it were bones are broken, while the strength of patience is afflicted, at which the wicked laugh. This is that reproach: *While it is said to me: Where is he?* either there is none, or he cares not for thee.

notes.text: But before faith — That is, the gospel dispensation. Came, we were kept - As in close custody. Under the law - The Mosaic dispensation. Shut up unto the faith which was to be revealed - Reserved and prepared for the gospel dispensation.

Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster unto Christ — It was designed to train us up for Christ. And this it did both by its commands, which showed the need we had of his atonement; and its ceremonies, which all pointed us to him.
But faith — That is, the gospel dispensation. Being come, we are no longer under that schoolmaster - The Mosaic dispensation.
For ye — Christians. Are all adult sons of God - And so need a schoolmaster no longer.
For as many of you as have testified your faith by being baptized in the name of Christ, have put on Christ — Have received him as your righteousness, and are therefore sons of God through him.

There is neither Jew nor Greek — That is, there is no difference between them; they are equally accepted through faith. There is neither male nor female - Circumcision being laid aside, which was peculiar to males, and was designed to put a difference, during that dispensation, between Jews and gentiles.
If ye are Christ's — That is, believers in him.

glossa.text: *Before that.* Before the coming of faith the law was useful to the Jews. *Faith came.* Faith is unbidden, which no merit called forth. *We were kept.* Not free, but servants. *Shut up.* That being thus accustomed we might be led. *Unto it.* That is, unto so good a faith. *Which.* It was in the time of Christ. *To be revealed.* In the time of Christ many things were opened which before were obscure. Behold the honour of the law: because it kept us as a pedagogue: but this is not a great thing, because this belongs to children, not to grown men.

*Was our pedagogue in Christ Jesus.* By the instruction of Christ: who therefore instructed, that so, coming to faith as children unto perfection, we might be justified. Or *in Christ,* that is, in the carrying out of the precepts of Christ.

*You are all children of God by faith.* We Jews in the time of faith forsook the pedagogue: because all you Gentiles, who had not the law, are sons. Do you then take up what we forsook by your example? As if he should say: You ought not to do this. *In Christ Jesus.* In the instruction of Christ, and unto the likeness of his death.

*You have put on.* That is, you have been made conformable to him, which is to you an honour and a protection against the heats. But that Christ is a garment, the Apostle elsewhere makes plain, saying: *Put ye on our Lord Jesus Christ.* Now men put on Christ: sometimes as far as the receiving of the sacrament: sometimes even as far as the sanctification of life. And that first is common to the good and to the evil. But this second is proper to the good.

*Then are you the seed of Abraham.* Christ was called the seed of Abraham: where it is read that the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. But here the sons of Christ, that is, all believers, are called the seed of Abraham. But as often as Christ is named the seed of Abraham, it is to be understood bodily: namely, that he is begotten of his stock. But as often as we who believe in him are called the seed of Abraham, then we ought spiritually to take the seed of faith.

notes.text: Matt. viii, 28; Mark v, 1.
For many times it had caught him — Therefore our compassionate Lord made the more haste to cast him out.
The abyss — That is, the bottomless pit.
To enter into the swine — Not that they were any easier in the swine than out of them. Had it been so, they would not so soon have dislodged themselves, by destroying the herd.
Matt. ix, 1; Mark v, 18.

glossa.text: *In the sepulchres.* What else are the bodies of the faithless but certain tombs of the dead, in which the words of God do not dwell?

*Jesus, Son of God.* Arius contends that he is a creature, whom the demon confesses to be the Son of God. The Jews say: *In the prince of demons he casteth out demons,* whom the demons deny to have anything in common with themselves. It is a torment to the devil to cease from injuring a man, and by how much the longer he had possessed him, by so much the more hardly does he let him go. Let anyone therefore who has been injured by the devil take care to break his yoke quickly, because his dominion is escaped the more easily the more quickly it is escaped.

*He was bound with chains.* The chains and fetters are the hard and heavy laws of the Gentiles, by which, even in their commonwealth, sins were restrained. Yet when these laws were broken, they were led by desire to those crimes which exceeded common usage.

*Because many demons entered,* etc. The many demons which oppress one man signify the many cults of idolatry in one people of the Gentiles. On the contrary it is said: *The multitude of believers had one heart and one soul ((Act. IV))*. Whence fittingly in Babylon the unity of tongues was rent, and in Jerusalem it was made one.

*And they besought.* The demons knew that by the Lord's coming they were one day to be plunged into the abyss: not themselves foreseeing things to come, but recalling the things said of them by the prophets.

*A herd of swine.* The swine are men devoid of speech and of reason, given over to filthy deeds, feeding on the mountain of pride. And unless a man has lived after the manner of a swine, the devil receives no power over him, or receives it only for proving him, and not for destroying him.

*They fled and told it in the city and in the villages.* The herdsmen fled, because neither the philosophers of the Gentiles nor the rulers of the Synagogue can bring medicine to the perishing; and although they flee the Christian law, yet by being astonished and by wondering they proclaim its power.

*And they went out to see what was done, and they came to Jesus, and found the man,* etc. It signifies the multitude, delighted with its own comely life, indeed honouring the Christian religion, but unwilling to endure it, while they say that they cannot fulfil it. They wonder also at the faithful people healed of its former manner of life, and sitting at the Lord's feet, that is, with a sound judgment of mind beholding the footsteps of the Saviour which it is to follow, and clothed with the pursuits of the virtues which, being deceived, it had lost.

*And they besought him.* Conscious of their frailty, they judge themselves unworthy of the Lord's presence, not receiving the word of God, and not sustaining the weight of wisdom in a firm mind; and therefore he was not troublesome to them any longer, but returns, because he does not deign to heal the unwilling, but quickly leaves the weak, to whom he sees his own presence to be a burden.

*Return to thy house,* etc. Allegorically. After the remission of sins one must return into a good conscience, and must serve the Gospel, for the salvation of others also, that thereafter he may rest with Christ; lest, when he now wishes to be near with Christ, he neglect the mystery of preaching that is fitted to the deliverance of the brethren. Whence the Apostle: *I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ ((Philip. I))*, a thing much better, *but to abide in the flesh is needful for you.*

echoes.text: for all the land which you see, I will give to you, and to your offspring forever.
echoes.note: 'You are Abraham's seed and heirs according to promise' (v.29) recapitulates the singular-seed promise of Gen 13:15/17:8 expounded in v.16, now extended to all who are Christ's. This closes the chapter's inclusio on seed/promise/inheritance with strong intra-chapter recurrence.

echoes.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
echoes.note: 'There is neither... male nor female' (v.28) verbally echoes Gen 1:27 LXX 'male and female he created them' (arsen kai thely), the only place this exact pairing occurs. Paul's shift from 'nor/nor' to 'and' marks the deliberate citation; the new creation in Christ relativizes the created distinction. Medium-high volume on the specific phrase.

echoes.text: All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your seed, because you have obeyed my voice.”
echoes.note: The heirs-of-promise climax (v.29) realizes the seed-and-nations blessing of Gen 22:18, gathering Gentile believers into Abraham's offspring. It reprises the citation chain (vv.8, 16) and so coheres with the chapter's argument, though without fresh wording. Medium.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'Put on Christ' (v.27) may echo the clothing-with-salvation imagery of Isa 61:10 ('he has clothed me with garments of salvation') and the robing motif of Zechariah 3:4. The metaphor of investiture is available in the prophets but the contact is thematic, not verbal. Contested and faint.

echoes.text: “I am inquired of by those who didn’t ask; I am found by those who didn’t seek me: I said, See me, see me, to a nation that was not called by my name. I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts; a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks; who sit among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat pig’s flesh, […]
echoes.note: Isaiah's rebellious people 'who sit in tombs and lodge in secret places, who eat swine's flesh' and say 'keep to yourself, do not come near me' map strikingly onto the demoniac among the tombs, the herd of swine, and the man's cry 'what have I to do with you?' The cluster of tombs + swine + repulsion gives notable Volume.

echoes.text: who sit among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat pig’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
echoes.note: The specific verse pairing dwelling among the tombs with eating swine's flesh concentrates the two defining impurities of the scene. Coherence with Luke's Gentile-territory unclean-spirit setting is strong.

echoes.text: The pig, because he has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, he is unclean to you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; they are unclean to you.
echoes.note: The classification of the pig as unclean (do not eat, do not touch its carcass) gives the swine their symbolic charge as fit vessels for unclean spirits in this Gentile region. Coherence is strong even though Luke does not cite the law.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: The demons' dread of the 'abyss' (8:31) evokes the primordial deep (LXX abyssos in Gen 1:2) as the place of chaos/restraint; the swine drowning in the lake returns the chaotic powers to the watery abyss. Conceptual, contested.

echoes.text: Save me from the lion’s mouth! Yes, from the horns of the wild oxen, you have answered me.
echoes.note: The cry of one tormented, naked, and bound, delivered by God, faintly resonates with the psalmist's plea for rescue from beastly powers; the 'Most High God' title also recurs in the psalms. Low Volume; contested.

echoes.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace: he spoke and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out, and come here. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the midst of the fire.
echoes.note: The Gentile address of God as 'the Most High God' (8:28) matches the Aramaic court-tale title used by Nebuchadnezzar, a Septuagintal idiom for the God of Israel on pagan lips. Real but minor lexical contact.

notes.text: I am, &c. — This in the primary sense of this text, is a prophecy of the conversion of the Gentiles, upon the rejection of the Jews; for their contempt and crucifying of Christ, cannot be doubted by any, who will not arrogate to themselves a greater ability to interpret the prophesies of the Old Testament, than St. Paul had, who, Rom. x, 20, expressly so interprets it, and applies it, which shews the vanity of the Jews in their other interpretations of it. Sought - The word signifies properly a diligent enquiry in things relating to God. Asked not - That in times past made no enquiry after me; l am now found by them that formerly sought me not. I said - I invited whole nations by the preaching of my gospel to behold me, and that with importunity, doubling my words upon them, and this I did unto a nation not called by my name, with whom I was not in covenant.

I have spread — Applied to the Jews, Rom. x, 21. I have stretched out my hands, I have used all means to reduce them, I have stretched out the hands of a passionate orator to persuade them, of a liberal benefactor to load them with my benefits; this I have done continually in the whole course of my providence with them.
To my face — With the utmost impudence, not taking notice of God's omnipresence, and omniscience. In gardens, &c. - Directly contrary to the divine rule.

Remain — They remained among the graves, there consulting with devils, who were thought to delight in such places; or to practice necromancy, all which were forbidden, Deut. xviii, 11 chap. viii, 19. Monuments - Some interpret it of idol temples, some of caves and dens, in which the Heathens used to worship their idols. Broth of abominable things - Of such flesh as was to the Jews unclean by the law.

Holier — Thus they esteemed themselves holier than others, though all their holiness lay in rituals, and those too, such as God never commanded. Of these God saith, These are a smoak in my nostrils, a fire that burneth all the day; that is, a continual provocation to me: as smoak is an offense to our noses.
Behold — They may think I take no notice of these things; but I will as certainly remember them, as princes or great men that record things in writing which they would not forget.

Together — Yea, and when I reckon with them, I will punish them, not only for their personal sins, but for the sins of their parents, which they have made their own, by imitation. Their former - I will not only punish the late sins that they have committed, but the former sins of this kind, which those that went before did commit, and they have continued in.

Thus, &c. — These word's may be conceived as a gracious answer from God to the prophet, pleading God's covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Israel. To this God replies, that he intended no such severity. His threatening should be made good upon the generality of this people. Blessing - But yet, as in a vineyard, which is generally unfruitful, there may be some vine that brings forth fruit, and has the hopes of new wine in the cluster, and as to such, the gardener bids his servant destroy it not, for there is in them what speaks God's blessing. So - So (saith God) will I do for my servants sake, that I may not destroy them all, for the sake of my servants, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

Judah — God farther promises to bring out of Judah, an inheritor of his mountains which refers to the Jews return out of the captivity of Babylon to Jerusalem, to worship God in his temple, upon Mount Zion. Mine elect - My chosen ones. The term signifies such as are dignified with some special favour. The whole nation of the Jews are called a chosen people.

glossa.text: *They have sought,* etc. ((HIER.)) To this the Son answers, etc., *as far as* and *The children that are strangers have lied to me ((Psal. XVII))*.
*I have spread forth my hands.* ((ID.)) Praying on the cross for them, etc., *as far as* yet they themselves were always unbelieving.

*A people that to anger.* ((ID.)) Allegorically. Every heretic solicits God to anger *procat*; read *provocat*, "provokes", etc., *as far as* and to build four-square, and to strengthen with lines the dust cut upon the brick.

*In the shrines.* *Delubra* are so called from *delendo*, blotting out, because there the soul was thought to be washed away. Or, because near by were the pools where both the priest and the victim were washed. Allegorically. ((HIER.)) Heretics in the memorials of their masters, etc., *as far as* so that whoever has not been like to them they detest as one lost.

*In my fury.* Fury, forgetfulness, anger, repentance, we ought so to take in God as we take hands, feet, eyes, ears, and the other members which he is said to have: not that he yields to these perturbations who extinguishes them in us, but through our own words; we understand God's disposition toward us.

*I will not be silent.* He who said above: *I have been silent, I have always held my peace, I have been patient,* now says: *I will not be silent,* that is, that I yield no longer, nor will I bear their iniquities.

*The iniquities of the fathers,* etc. So that, namely, you may be punished not only for your own sins, but also for the iniquities of the fathers whom you have imitated. For otherwise the son does not bear the iniquity of the father. *Who have sacrificed upon the mountains.* When in Bethel and in Dan they adored the golden calves. The heretic also, contemning the simplicity of the Church, sacrifices upon the mountains, and upbraids God while he contemns his precepts.
*As.* ((HIER.)) As if he should say: For the sake of the wicked I will not destroy the good: *But as,* etc. For he had said that Israel should perish.

*Out of Jacob a seed.* The seed of Jacob and of Juda, the apostles, possessing the mountains, that is, others, namely believers eminent in the virtues: whence, *Unless the Lord of Sabaoth had left us a seed, we had been as Sodom ((Rom. IX))*. *My holy mountains.* The Septuagint: *My mountain,* namely Christ, who is the mountain of mountains. For the mountains are the apostles, who out of the Jews possessed Christ, in whom they are founded. *And they shall inherit.* ((HIER.)) Whence: *The seed of Abraham his servant: the sons of Jacob, his elect.* Whosoever are still seed, etc., *as far as you have not received the spirit of bondage again in fear, but you have received the spirit of the adoption of the sons of God ((Rom. IX))*.

notes.text: Darling — Hebrew. my only one; his soul, which he so calls, because it was left alone and destitute of friends and helpers.
Heard — Answered and delivered me.

Declare — When thou hast delivered me. Thy name - that power and faithfulness and goodness, which thou hast manifested on my behalf. Congregations - The same whom he calls the congregation, and the seed of Jacob and Israel: which also does not so fitly agree to David, who never gives this title to any, but such as were near a-kin to him, as it does to Christ, who extends this name to all his disciples, Matt. xii, 48, 49, and to whom this very text is applied, Heb. ii, 11, 12.
Abhorred — He did not turn away his face from it, as men do from things which they abhor. From him - For ever: tho' he did so for a time.
Great congregation — In the universal church, of Jews and Gentiles.

Satisfied — This is doubtless to be understood, of those spiritual blessings, that grace and peace, and comfort, which all believing souls have in the sense of God's love, the pardon of their sins, and the influences of God's spirit. Seek him - That seek his favour. Your heart - He speaks of the same persons still, though there be a change from the third to the second person, as is usual in these poetical books. For ever - Your comfort shall not be short and transitory, as worldly comforts are, but everlasting.

The world — All nations from one end of the world to the other. So this is an evident prophecy of the calling of the Gentiles, and a clear proof, that this psalm immediately speaks of Christ; to whom alone, this and divers other passages of it, belong. Remember - They shall remember their former wickedness with grief and shame, and fear; particularly in worshiping dead and impotent idols. They shall remember their great and manifold obligation to God, which they had quite forgotten, his patience in sparing them so long, in the midst of all their impieties, and in giving his son for them: they shall remember the gracious words and glorious works of Christ, what he did, and suffered for them; which possibly divers of them had been eye and ear-witnesses of. The Lord - Into the only true God, and unto Jesus Christ, to whom this name of Jehovah is often ascribed in scripture.
For — This is added as a reason, why the Gentiles should be converted, because God is not only God and the Lord of the Jews, but also of the Gentiles, and of all nations.

glossa.text: *From the unicorns, my lowness,* etc. ((ID.)) The Jews, seeking earthly things only: or, boasting themselves singularly of the worship of God, or being singularly proud, the son also having been slain after the servants.
*Ye that fear the Lord, praise him,* etc. ((CASS.)) Human fear brings forth not praise, but blame.

*Let all the seed of Israel fear him, because he hath not despised,* etc. Whom he means by the seed of Jacob he opens, adding: *Of the poor man.* ((AUG.)) Not of him who cries out with the words of sins out of a vain life, but of him who is not swollen with the pomps of the world.
*With thee is my praise in a great church,* etc. ((ID.)) He places his praise with God, who teaches that there be no presuming in man.

*They shall praise the Lord that seek him: they shall live.* ((ID.)) The poor are rich in God: therefore poor, because they praise God that they may seek him, and he himself is the riches of the poor. *Their hearts shall remember for ever and ever, and shall be converted to the Lord.* ((ID.)) Because he is the food of the heart.

notes.text: But before faith — That is, the gospel dispensation. Came, we were kept - As in close custody. Under the law - The Mosaic dispensation. Shut up unto the faith which was to be revealed - Reserved and prepared for the gospel dispensation.

Wherefore the law was our schoolmaster unto Christ — It was designed to train us up for Christ. And this it did both by its commands, which showed the need we had of his atonement; and its ceremonies, which all pointed us to him.
But faith — That is, the gospel dispensation. Being come, we are no longer under that schoolmaster - The Mosaic dispensation.
For ye — Christians. Are all adult sons of God - And so need a schoolmaster no longer.
For as many of you as have testified your faith by being baptized in the name of Christ, have put on Christ — Have received him as your righteousness, and are therefore sons of God through him.

There is neither Jew nor Greek — That is, there is no difference between them; they are equally accepted through faith. There is neither male nor female - Circumcision being laid aside, which was peculiar to males, and was designed to put a difference, during that dispensation, between Jews and gentiles.
If ye are Christ's — That is, believers in him.

glossa.text: *Before that.* Before the coming of faith the law was useful to the Jews. *Faith came.* Faith is unbidden, which no merit called forth. *We were kept.* Not free, but servants. *Shut up.* That being thus accustomed we might be led. *Unto it.* That is, unto so good a faith. *Which.* It was in the time of Christ. *To be revealed.* In the time of Christ many things were opened which before were obscure. Behold the honour of the law: because it kept us as a pedagogue: but this is not a great thing, because this belongs to children, not to grown men.

*Was our pedagogue in Christ Jesus.* By the instruction of Christ: who therefore instructed, that so, coming to faith as children unto perfection, we might be justified. Or *in Christ,* that is, in the carrying out of the precepts of Christ.

*You are all children of God by faith.* We Jews in the time of faith forsook the pedagogue: because all you Gentiles, who had not the law, are sons. Do you then take up what we forsook by your example? As if he should say: You ought not to do this. *In Christ Jesus.* In the instruction of Christ, and unto the likeness of his death.

*You have put on.* That is, you have been made conformable to him, which is to you an honour and a protection against the heats. But that Christ is a garment, the Apostle elsewhere makes plain, saying: *Put ye on our Lord Jesus Christ.* Now men put on Christ: sometimes as far as the receiving of the sacrament: sometimes even as far as the sanctification of life. And that first is common to the good and to the evil. But this second is proper to the good.

*Then are you the seed of Abraham.* Christ was called the seed of Abraham: where it is read that the promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. But here the sons of Christ, that is, all believers, are called the seed of Abraham. But as often as Christ is named the seed of Abraham, it is to be understood bodily: namely, that he is begotten of his stock. But as often as we who believe in him are called the seed of Abraham, then we ought spiritually to take the seed of faith.

notes.text: Matt. viii, 28; Mark v, 1.
For many times it had caught him — Therefore our compassionate Lord made the more haste to cast him out.
The abyss — That is, the bottomless pit.
To enter into the swine — Not that they were any easier in the swine than out of them. Had it been so, they would not so soon have dislodged themselves, by destroying the herd.
Matt. ix, 1; Mark v, 18.

glossa.text: *In the sepulchres.* What else are the bodies of the faithless but certain tombs of the dead, in which the words of God do not dwell?

*Jesus, Son of God.* Arius contends that he is a creature, whom the demon confesses to be the Son of God. The Jews say: *In the prince of demons he casteth out demons,* whom the demons deny to have anything in common with themselves. It is a torment to the devil to cease from injuring a man, and by how much the longer he had possessed him, by so much the more hardly does he let him go. Let anyone therefore who has been injured by the devil take care to break his yoke quickly, because his dominion is escaped the more easily the more quickly it is escaped.

*He was bound with chains.* The chains and fetters are the hard and heavy laws of the Gentiles, by which, even in their commonwealth, sins were restrained. Yet when these laws were broken, they were led by desire to those crimes which exceeded common usage.

*Because many demons entered,* etc. The many demons which oppress one man signify the many cults of idolatry in one people of the Gentiles. On the contrary it is said: *The multitude of believers had one heart and one soul ((Act. IV))*. Whence fittingly in Babylon the unity of tongues was rent, and in Jerusalem it was made one.

*And they besought.* The demons knew that by the Lord's coming they were one day to be plunged into the abyss: not themselves foreseeing things to come, but recalling the things said of them by the prophets.

*A herd of swine.* The swine are men devoid of speech and of reason, given over to filthy deeds, feeding on the mountain of pride. And unless a man has lived after the manner of a swine, the devil receives no power over him, or receives it only for proving him, and not for destroying him.

*They fled and told it in the city and in the villages.* The herdsmen fled, because neither the philosophers of the Gentiles nor the rulers of the Synagogue can bring medicine to the perishing; and although they flee the Christian law, yet by being astonished and by wondering they proclaim its power.

*And they went out to see what was done, and they came to Jesus, and found the man,* etc. It signifies the multitude, delighted with its own comely life, indeed honouring the Christian religion, but unwilling to endure it, while they say that they cannot fulfil it. They wonder also at the faithful people healed of its former manner of life, and sitting at the Lord's feet, that is, with a sound judgment of mind beholding the footsteps of the Saviour which it is to follow, and clothed with the pursuits of the virtues which, being deceived, it had lost.

*And they besought him.* Conscious of their frailty, they judge themselves unworthy of the Lord's presence, not receiving the word of God, and not sustaining the weight of wisdom in a firm mind; and therefore he was not troublesome to them any longer, but returns, because he does not deign to heal the unwilling, but quickly leaves the weak, to whom he sees his own presence to be a burden.

*Return to thy house,* etc. Allegorically. After the remission of sins one must return into a good conscience, and must serve the Gospel, for the salvation of others also, that thereafter he may rest with Christ; lest, when he now wishes to be near with Christ, he neglect the mystery of preaching that is fitted to the deliverance of the brethren. Whence the Apostle: *I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ ((Philip. I))*, a thing much better, *but to abide in the flesh is needful for you.*

echoes.text: for all the land which you see, I will give to you, and to your offspring forever.
echoes.note: 'You are Abraham's seed and heirs according to promise' (v.29) recapitulates the singular-seed promise of Gen 13:15/17:8 expounded in v.16, now extended to all who are Christ's. This closes the chapter's inclusio on seed/promise/inheritance with strong intra-chapter recurrence.

echoes.text: God created man in his own image. In God’s image he created him; male and female he created them.
echoes.note: 'There is neither... male nor female' (v.28) verbally echoes Gen 1:27 LXX 'male and female he created them' (arsen kai thely), the only place this exact pairing occurs. Paul's shift from 'nor/nor' to 'and' marks the deliberate citation; the new creation in Christ relativizes the created distinction. Medium-high volume on the specific phrase.

echoes.text: All the nations of the earth will be blessed by your seed, because you have obeyed my voice.”
echoes.note: The heirs-of-promise climax (v.29) realizes the seed-and-nations blessing of Gen 22:18, gathering Gentile believers into Abraham's offspring. It reprises the citation chain (vv.8, 16) and so coheres with the chapter's argument, though without fresh wording. Medium.

echoes.text: I will greatly rejoice in Yahweh, my soul shall be joyful in my God; for he has clothed me with the garments of salvation, he has covered me with the robe of righteousness, as a bridegroom decks himself with a garland, and as a bride adorns herself with her jewels.
echoes.note: 'Put on Christ' (v.27) may echo the clothing-with-salvation imagery of Isa 61:10 ('he has clothed me with garments of salvation') and the robing motif of Zechariah 3:4. The metaphor of investiture is available in the prophets but the contact is thematic, not verbal. Contested and faint.

echoes.text: “I am inquired of by those who didn’t ask; I am found by those who didn’t seek me: I said, See me, see me, to a nation that was not called by my name. I have spread out my hands all the day to a rebellious people, who walk in a way that is not good, after their own thoughts; a people who provoke me to my face continually, sacrificing in gardens, and burning incense on bricks; who sit among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat pig’s flesh, […]
echoes.note: Isaiah's rebellious people 'who sit in tombs and lodge in secret places, who eat swine's flesh' and say 'keep to yourself, do not come near me' map strikingly onto the demoniac among the tombs, the herd of swine, and the man's cry 'what have I to do with you?' The cluster of tombs + swine + repulsion gives notable Volume.

echoes.text: who sit among the graves, and lodge in the secret places; who eat pig’s flesh, and broth of abominable things is in their vessels;
echoes.note: The specific verse pairing dwelling among the tombs with eating swine's flesh concentrates the two defining impurities of the scene. Coherence with Luke's Gentile-territory unclean-spirit setting is strong.

echoes.text: The pig, because he has a split hoof, and is cloven-footed, but doesn’t chew the cud, he is unclean to you. Of their flesh you shall not eat, and their carcasses you shall not touch; they are unclean to you.
echoes.note: The classification of the pig as unclean (do not eat, do not touch its carcass) gives the swine their symbolic charge as fit vessels for unclean spirits in this Gentile region. Coherence is strong even though Luke does not cite the law.

echoes.text: The earth was formless and empty. Darkness was on the surface of the deep and God’s Spirit was hovering over the surface of the waters.
echoes.note: The demons' dread of the 'abyss' (8:31) evokes the primordial deep (LXX abyssos in Gen 1:2) as the place of chaos/restraint; the swine drowning in the lake returns the chaotic powers to the watery abyss. Conceptual, contested.

echoes.text: Save me from the lion’s mouth! Yes, from the horns of the wild oxen, you have answered me.
echoes.note: The cry of one tormented, naked, and bound, delivered by God, faintly resonates with the psalmist's plea for rescue from beastly powers; the 'Most High God' title also recurs in the psalms. Low Volume; contested.

echoes.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar came near to the mouth of the burning fiery furnace: he spoke and said, Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego, you servants of the Most High God, come out, and come here. Then Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego came out of the midst of the fire.
echoes.note: The Gentile address of God as 'the Most High God' (8:28) matches the Aramaic court-tale title used by Nebuchadnezzar, a Septuagintal idiom for the God of Israel on pagan lips. Real but minor lexical contact.

registers.label: Spare
lines: As a deer longs for flowing streams, so we have come, thirsty for God.
Why are you cast down, my soul? Hope in God.
We came from the tombs and the noise, like the man Jesus set free.
He has clothed us, and given us back our right minds.
Out of the wind and the fire came a sound of sheer silence — the voice of God.
Speak, Lord; we are listening.
Come, let us worship, and tell what God has done.
We will declare how much God has done for us. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Picture a deer at the end of a long dry day, picking its way down to the streambed — that is your soul, thirsty, leaning toward living water.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise.
Some of us come worn down, like Elijah under the broom tree, ready to give up — and the angel says, get up and eat, the way is long.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise.
Some of us come like the man among the tombs, and Jesus speaks, and the chains fall, and we are in our right minds at his feet.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise.
So bring your thirst and your tears to the stream this morning. Drink deep, and tell the mercy you have found.
Hope in God; we shall again give praise. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Thirsty as a deer for the stream, we come.
Hope in God.
From the tombs and the chains, Jesus has set us free.
Hope in God.
In wind and fire, a quiet voice still calls.
Hope in God.
Come, drink deep, and worship.
Hope in God, who is our help. Amen.
